articles.title: Rio entra em estágio 2 pelo esquema operacional para o Rock in Rio; fãs aguardam abertura dos portões da Cidade do Rock
articles.summary: Rio entra em estágio 2 pelo esquema operacional para o Rock in Rio; fãs aguardam abertura dos portões da Cidade do Rock
articles.body:
Festival começa nesta sexta (4), com Foo Fighters; veja programação

O que pode e o que não pode levar para a Cidade do Rock? Veja

Primeira parte dos portões é aberta na Cidade do Rock. Fãs aguardam na grade para entrar no Rock in Rio.

A cidade do Rio de Janeiro entrou em Estágio 2 às 12h desta sexta-feira (4) em função do esquema operacional para o Rock in Rio e a mudança de rotina da cidade, com a antecipação no horário de saída em repartições públicas.

O Estágio 2 é o segundo nível em uma escala de cinco e significa que há previsão de mudança na rotina da cidade.

Fãs do The Hives, segunda atração do Palco Mundo nesta sexta-feira (4), aguardam a abertura dos portões da Cidade do Rock.

Em dia de sol forte, os fãs aguardam a abertura dos portões do Rock in Rio em uma fila, aproveitando a sombra de um poste.

Artistas que se apresentarão no palco Supernova fazem os últimos ensaios antes dos shows.

A Cidade do Rock está pronta para receber cerca de 100 mil fãs de música por dia. Confira as imagens do Parque Olímpico pronto para a abertura dos portões.

Roberta e Liz montaram uma espécie de barraca usando a estrutura de uma caçamba de lixo antes da abertura dos portões do Rock in Rio. As duas se conheceram em um grupo de mulheres criado para reunir fãs que vão juntas a shows. “Carioca, né? A gente tenta se proteger como pode. Ficar no sol, no osso, não dá” disse Liz.

Os fãs da banda Foo Fighters chegaram cedo aos portões da Cidade do Rock. Eles fizeram uma fila por ordem de chegada. Veja mais aqui.

Quem for ao Rock in Rio 2026 e quiser comer dentro da cidade do rock, no Parque Olímpico, vai encontrar opções para diferentes gostos e bolsos. Os preços dos restaurantes do festival variam de R$12 a R$80, considerando os itens e combos listados nos cardápios. Quer planejar o que vai comer? Confira a reportagem completa.

O Palco Mundo, o principal do festival, contará com um telão de 2,4 mil metros quadrados para o vento. De acordo com Roberta Medina, vice-presidente da Rock World, o espaço vai ganhar a cara do artista que estiver se apresentando. Veja mais.

O Rock in Rio 2026 começa nesta sexta-feira (4). Aqui você não perde nada do que acontece na Cidade do Rock. Confira a programação do festival .

articles.title: Kai Trump reveals she's not 'eaten in 3 days' following major upheaval in personal life
articles.summary: Kai Trump documented her first week at the University of Miami with an emotional video shared to her YouTube – see details
articles.body:
President Donald Trump's granddaughter, Kai Trump, recently shared her emotional struggle with adjusting to college life at the University of Miami.

Kai documented her first week at college in a YouTube video, where she tearfully said goodbye to her family and friends before returning home due to illness.

The 19-year-old, who is a golf enthusiast, is one of five children of Vanessa and Donald Trump Jr., who divorced in 2018 but continue to co-parent their kids amicably.

President Donald Trump's granddaughter, Kai Trump , has opened up about struggling to adjust to college life as she began her first week at the University of Miami. The 19-year-old, who is in her freshman year, documented her experience in a new video shared on her YouTube channel.

In the vlog, Kai filmed herself driving home from the golf course the day she left her home in Jupiter, Florida, for school. "It's just really sad that I have to say goodbye to everyone today," she said with tears in her eyes.

"I'm not a very emotional person at all, so this is like really weird for me to cry, I've only cried a few times. I think knowing that I have to say goodbye to everyone tonight really, really sucks."

She continued: "I don't have to say goodbye to my mom tomorrow, but [saying goodbye to] everybody else [tonight] is sad. I'm struggling right now, just thinking about it." However, Kai added that she was "excited" for her next chapter but "emotional" about it.

Later in the video, Kai showed off her new Miami apartment and documented her first week attending golf practice and class. Kai's friend, Emma, visited her apartment and brought the teen lots of frozen food, as she shared that she "hadn't eaten in three days."

"It's all pre-cooked so she doesn't have to do anything crazy," said Emma. "She's living off of diet sodas, so I got her fruit and prosciutto and we got her some pasta and bread and stuff, like basic foods, she's basically living off of diet soda."

Kai's first week at college was cut short as she was forced to return home after suffering from Strep throat. "I got sick with Strep on Wednesday, my first week of school," she shared. "I came all the way back to Jupiter because I was so sick I needed my mom to nurse me back to health."

Kai is one out of five of Vanessa and Donald Trump Jr.'s children. The couple tied the knot back in 2005 and share Kai Madison, Donald Trump III, Tristan Milos, Spencer Frederick, and Chloe Sophia. The pair divorced in 2018, but continue to amicably co-parent their kids.

The teen is a golf enthusiast and has been playing the sport for over 13 years. "Golf has always been a massive part of my life and is my biggest passion. I always aspire to be a leader and a positive figure on and off the golf course," she previously shared.

articles.title: Evento gratuito em Sarapuí une esporte e história neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento gratuito terá duas opções de trajeto pela zona rural do município. Os trajetos buscam unir esporte e turismo rural. Os ciclistas passarão por propriedades e cerca de 25 capelas históricas.
articles.summary: A 1ª Ciclorrota da Fé em Sarapuí oferece trajetos gratuitos de até 79 km por propriedades rurais e igrejas históricas, promovendo o turismo e o esporte na região.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Sarapuí (SP) promove, neste domingo (6), a 1ª edição da Ciclorrota da Fé com dois percursos pela zona rural do município: um de 23 quilômetros e outro de 79 quilômetros. As inscrições são gratuitas e devem ser feitas pelo site .

A proposta é unir esporte, turismo e cultura, permitindo que moradores e visitantes conheçam paisagens rurais, propriedades, áreas de mata e pontos históricos da cidade. A largada será às 8h30, em frente à Igreja Matriz Nossa Senhora das Dores.

Ao g1 , Marcio José Ricardo Sturaro, diretor municipal de Sarapuí, disse que os dois trajetos foram pensados para atender diferentes perfis de participantes.

"O percurso de 23 km é uma opção mais curta para quem está começando ou não está acostumado a percorrer longas distâncias. Já o percurso de 79 km oferece um desafio maior para quem busca uma experiência mais longa de ciclismo."

Além da diferença de distância, os caminhos também são distintos. O percurso mais longo passa por um número maior de bairros e pontos de interesse, incluindo capelas e igrejas históricas espalhadas pela zona rural.

"O passeio é uma oportunidade de apresentar Sarapuí por meio de seus caminhos rurais, sua história e seus espaços de importância cultural. Muitas das capelas e igrejas encontradas pelo trajeto têm mais de 100 anos e fazem parte da história das comunidades do município", explica Sturaro.

Capela São Roque, de 1932, em Sarapuí, é um dos pontos visitados durante o trajeto — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

Ao todo, cerca de 25 igrejas e capelas podem ser observadas ao longo dos percursos, embora a quantidade varie de acordo com o trajeto escolhido .

"Uma equipe acompanhará o percurso e auxiliará na orientação dos participantes. Algumas capelas estarão diretamente no caminho e poderão ser identificadas durante o trajeto. Já aquelas localizadas fora da rota principal serão indicadas, permitindo que cada participante decida se deseja fazer o desvio para conhecê-las", relata o diretor municipal.

Igrejas e capelas podem ser observadas ao longo dos percursos percorridos de bicicleta em Sarapuí (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

Além das construções religiosas, os ciclistas terão contato com diferentes características da vida rural de Sarapuí, como propriedades, animais, áreas de cultivo, casarões antigos e estabelecimentos existentes ao longo das estradas.

"O município está inserido predominantemente no bioma Mata Atlântica, com áreas de transição entre a Mata Atlântica e o Cerrado. Durante o trajeto, os participantes poderão observar áreas de mata, estradas rurais, regiões próximas a cursos d'água e outras paisagens naturais", detalha Maurício.

Evento de ciclismo em Sarapuí (SP) passará por propriedades rurais e construções religiosas — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

A prefeitura informou que uma equipe da administração municipal estará presente durante o percurso para orientar os participantes. O trajeto será sinalizado e contará com indicações dos principais pontos de interesse e locais de parada.

Todos os ciclistas receberão uma medalha ao final do percurso.

Os participantes também podem doar 1 litro de leite, que será arrecadado pela organização e encaminhado ao Fundo Social de Solidariedade de Sarapuí. Os donativos serão destinados a famílias que necessitam de assistência.

Segundo a prefeitura, a proposta surgiu a partir da ideia de utilizar o ciclismo como uma maneira de conhecer e valorizar diferentes regiões de Sarapuí, especialmente os caminhos e atrativos existentes na zona rural.

"Sarapuí faz parte da região turística Veredas da Mata Atlântica, que trabalha com a proposta de fortalecer o turismo regional e desenvolver roteiros que integrem os municípios da região. O percurso utiliza esses espaços como pontos de interesse, unindo a prática esportiva ao conhecimento da história e da cultura local", comenta o diretor municipal.

O evento não integra, ainda, um programa estadual específico. Segundo a prefeitura, a iniciativa foi criada pelo próprio município após a administração observar projetos semelhantes desenvolvidos por outras cidades da região turística.

Percurso mais longo passa por um número maior de bairros e pontos de interesse, incluindo capelas e igrejas históricas espalhadas pela zona rural de Sarapuí (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

De acordo com a prefeitura, o município vem adotando medidas para ampliar sua participação no cenário turístico regional e nacional.

Entre as ações estão a criação de uma estrutura específica para o turismo, com assessor da área, e a previsão de um cargo efetivo de tecnólogo em turismo, por meio de concurso público.

O município também encaminhou a documentação necessária para buscar o título de Município de Interesse Turístico (MIT) junto à Secretaria de Turismo e Viagens. Sarapuí também integra o Mapa do Turismo Brasileiro, do Ministério do Turismo.

Sarapuí tem quase um búfalo para cada dois moradores — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Sarapuí

Além da Ciclorrota, a administração mantém iniciativas como o projeto Pé na Roça, Boia Cross, Feira Livre, Feira da Lua e Festival do Búfalo.

"Também está sendo desenvolvido um trabalho de resgate do patrimônio histórico, com destaque para o casario colonial e a história relacionada ao tropeirismo. Outros levantamentos e ações de resgate histórico também estão sendo estudados, incluindo aspectos da história religiosa ligada a João de Camargo e a história das comunidades quilombolas e do caxambu no bairro dos Cocaes", concluiu o diretor municipal.

Município de Sarapuí (SP) realiza torneio de pesca — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura Municipal de Sarapuí

No Centro de Sarapuí, os três imóveis ficam a apenas 600 metros de distância um do outro. O primeiro, localizado na Rua Doutor Cerqueira César, foi construído por imigrantes alemães e tem cerca de 126 anos. O segundo, na Rua Doutor Luiz Vergueiro, existe há 111 anos e foi utilizado como casa paroquial. Já o terceiro, na Rua Quintino Bocaiúva, foi erguido há mais de 140 anos.

O casarão na região central de Sarapuí foi construído entre 1850 e 1870 — Foto: João Paulo Netto/Arquivo pessoal

O professor, pesquisador e arquiteto Igor Chaves, de Itapetininga (SP), explica que os casarões precisam ser preservados, estudados e registrados, principalmente para que as novas gerações possam conhecer e compreender melhor o passado da cidade.

"A preservação de prédios históricos é fundamental não apenas por seu valor arquitetônico ou estético, mas sobretudo por aquilo que representam: são testemunhos vivos da história, das memórias coletivas e das formas de vida que moldaram a identidade de nossa cidade", apontou.

articles.summary: Responsáveis por menores de 16 anos podem registrar dados antes do festival e retirar pulseira de identificação nas entradas do evento.
articles.body:
Quem for ao Rock in Rio com crianças e adolescentes de até 16 anos poderá cadastrá-los em um sistema de identificação disponibilizado pela organização do festival. Segundo o evento, o objetivo é agilizar a localização dos responsáveis em casos de desencontro dentro da Cidade do Rock.

O cadastro deve ser feito previamente pela internet pelo site . Depois, já no local, os responsáveis precisam procurar os pontos de identificação nas entradas do festival para retirar uma pulseira destinada ao menor .

Para concluir o processo, é necessário vincular ao cadastro o número impresso na pulseira . Com isso, equipes do festival poderão consultar os contatos de emergência informados pelos responsáveis caso a criança ou adolescente se perca.

Cadastro deve ser feito pelo site — Foto: Reprodução

A organização recomenda que o registro seja realizado antes da chegada ao evento para evitar filas e agilizar o acesso ao sistema de identificação.

O Rock in Rio 2026 será transmitido ao vivo pelo Globoplay , Multishow e Bis . Na Globo , haverá entradas durante a programação e um programa especial, ao fim de cada noite, com os melhores momentos do festival.

Nesta sexta, a Fundação para a Infância e Adolescência (FIA), por meio do programa SOS Crianças Desaparecidas, realiza uma mobilização de orientação, informação e prevenção ao desaparecimento de crianças e adolescentes na estação do metrô da Central do Brasil e na rodoviária do Rio.

Durante a mobilização, equipes distribuem materiais informativos, orientar pais, responsáveis e familiares sobre medidas preventivas e realizar a identificação de crianças e adolescentes.

A iniciativa busca ampliar a conscientização das famílias sobre cuidados simples que podem contribuir para evitar situações de desaparecimento em locais de grande movimentação.

Entre os principais cuidados a serem tomados, recomenda-se que pais e responsáveis mantenham a criança sempre próxima, evitem que ela circule sozinha em locais de grande aglomeração e utilizem mecanismos de identificação, como pulseiras ou etiquetas com dados de contato, durante o evento.

articles.title: Birmingham music festival celebrates 20 year anniversary
articles.summary: The event, which has become a staple in the Midlands music diary, first appeared in 2006.
articles.body:
The Moseley Folk festival takes place this weekend with headliners Kingfishr, Super Furry Animals, and The Dead South all set to wow the crowds.

The event, which has become a staple in the Midlands music diary, first appeared in 2006.

It takes place in the secluded Moseley Park in Birmingham, and has seen headliners ranging from Donovan to Don Mclean, from Steeleye Span to Echo and the Bunnymen.

"It feels like your classic British festival in the countryside, but yet here it is right in the heart of the city, in this lush park, with a really cosy vibe", said Max Gittings, from folk group, The Destroyers.

He added: "We were just delighted to be invited."

Gittings' band, who hail from Birmingham, were well-received at the inaugural festival previously, due to their 'megafolk' style.

"We played this lovely chilled out afternoon set and it was among the first proper festivals we'd started to play at, the year before we did our first Glastonbury", he said.

The band have played at the festival many times since, and will be on stage again this year for the twentieth anniversary.

"It holds special memories, it was part of our beginnings.

"Just gathering at the lake backstage beforehand and then coming out to play for a really nice audience is great."

The Moseley Folk audience has grown from around 1,000 people two decades ago, to the 4,000 expected for 2026.

Festival organiser, John Fell, says that while the music is the key attraction, incorporating more food and drink has been an important step.

"Over the years we've changed by adding a few more stages, bringing in workshops, family areas...but the food scene in Birmingham has grown incredibly, so we've enveloped that as well and the crowds have got bigger and stronger every year."

Smaller boutique-style festivals have exploded across the UK in the last decade but they're not always easy to sustain.

Costs have inevitably risen, and with weekend tickets at £182 and day tickets £69 there are also some who could find it difficult to afford.

But Fell maintains it's very good value for what is being provided.

He says that the festival is passionate about supporting local artists and businesses.

"It's Brummies that run it. Everyone involved is local.

"That's a really proud thing for us to do because we have a national audience coming in seeing the best of Birmingham."

The twentieth edition of the Moseley Folk and Arts Festival incorporates aspects of comedy, poetry and wellness.

Twenty-nine acts played the first two-day festival in 2006, this year will see between 60 and 70 acts perform.

Fell thinks the event's legacy is secure.

He said: "There's so much going on in the world that live music is always going to be at the forefront of people wanting to get out there, experience [it] and have a good time.

"So thankfully we're involved in that process and I think we've got a good future to come."

articles.title: Barnsley travelling telephone box tells town's stories
articles.summary: A red telephone box which plays audio monologues from people in Barnsley is setting off on a tour.
articles.body:
A red telephone box which plays audio monologues of stories from people in Barnsley through a handset is setting off on a tour of the town.

The "Calling Barnsley" project was created by Lung Theatre group who recorded the monologues and built a life-sized phone box, which has been housed in the Barnsley Civic Arts Centre since January.

Now, the group is hoping to "share the stories" as the box embarks on a six-month tour of the town's libraries.

Matt Woodhead, theatre co-director, said, "There's a poeticism in the way that people in Barnsley speak. You can't knock about town without someone pulling your ear and telling you the most incredible story."

Co-director Helen Monks, said their box was wider than a typical public one in order to allow wheelchair access.

"Otherwise it looks the same. You still pick up the receiver and dial a different number depending on what story you want to hear," she explained.

The theatre group worked with students at Barnsley College to collect and record the two-minute stories through workshops over a two-year period.

The students also helped produce and direct vocal actors to transform them into monologues.

Woodhead said they managed to collect a "whole chocolate box" of stories.

He said: "We've got a gorgeous story about the Christmas lights of Thurnscoe, about how a community came together - and then, in contrast, the story of someone getting a kebab thrown at them when they're in town on a night out."

The kebab story was Dr Ryan Bramley's own personal experience as a student.

Now a lecturer in education at the University of Sheffield, Bramley, born in Barnsley was struck by a kebab on a night out because he was "wearing a smartish blazer".

The group managed to collect more than 60 stories in total, which were picked up by publishers Faber and Faber and turned into a book.

Monks said it was "the right time" for the phone box, which can be dismantled into five parts, to move.

"One of the things that we found is that people really see themselves as cultural people in Barnsley so it's really important that the phone doesn't just sit in the town centre but it goes to all of people's local areas".

From 4 September, the phone box's new home for a month will be The Lightbox at Barnsley Central Library before moving on to libraries in Royston, Cudworth, Atherley, Goldthorpe and Penistone over the next six months.

It will also be stopping at Persistence Works Sheffield as part of University of Sheffield's Festival of the Mind.

Woodhead said the long-term home for the phone box was unknown but that this was "just the start of a conversation".

"This phone box is a beautiful celebration of Barnsley but you also don't need the phone box to go and tell your story. There's so many people that have got a story to tell so you have to get right in and start telling it," he added.

articles.title: La tremenda pelea entre Marcos de Quinto y Afra Blanca en ‘Espejo Público’: “Cuando yo intervengo pone caritas de payasa”
articles.standfirst: El empresario y la sindicalista discuten en directo en el espacio de Antena 3
articles.summary: El empresario y la sindicalista discuten en directo en el espacio de Antena 3
articles.body: Este viernes, 4 de septiembre, el plató de ‘Espejo Público’ ha vivido una de las mayores broncas del año en el programa matinal de Antena 3 que presenta Susanna Griso. Mientras se debatía acerca de la crisis migratoria en Ceuta, Marcos de Quinto y Afra Blanco han protagonizado una pelea que ha obligado a intervenir a la conductora del espacio ante la sorpresa de todos los presentes. Todo ha ocurrido cuando Griso ha pedido a Blanco que hablara sobre los informes del CENIF, pero las primeras palabras de la sindicalista han ido dirigidas a su compañero: “Lamento tener que romper la dinámica del debate. He pasado todo el verano criticando la gestión de esta crisis, pero… Marcos, qué elegante te presentas aquí hoy, ¿eh?”. Ante el silencio del empresario, ha proseguido: “Pero después, Marcos de Quinto tiene otra versión. Supongo que la valentía y la gallardía se la ha dejado en el fondo de un botellín, en ese yate”. Tras ello, ha justificado su ataque por los supuestos insultos de su compañero en redes sociales: “Digo esto porque somos cinco mujeres en esta mesa, que discrepamos, que debatimos y que supongo que continuamente sufrimos ataques, denigración, cosificación e insultos en redes sociales”. Cuando Afra Blanco ha pedido a Marcos de Quinto que aplicara esa misma valentía en persona, el empresario no se ha quedado callado. “Continuamente, cuando yo intervengo en este programa, ella se pone a hacer caritas de payasa. Es una cosa que me disgusta”, ha aseverado. “Y yo tengo una pregunta para Afra: ¿Habéis devuelto los de la UGT los 40 millones que robasteis al fondo de parados en Andalucía y que está firme por sentencia del Tribunal Supremo?”, ha replicado el empresario, que ha zanjado: “Discúlpate por poner caritas. Afra, que eres una broncas, estás a broncas con todo el mundo”.

articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s school warning letters reignite privacy battle they ‘cannot control’: experts
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are reportedly starting private school in the Cotswolds, prompting warning letters to parents about privacy rules.
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s return to the United Kingdom could become their biggest privacy test yet as their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet begin school life in the English countryside. Last week, Markle, 45, and Harry, 41, along with their son Archie, 7, and daughter Princess Lilibet, 5, left their home in Montecito, California, for an extended stay in Britain. According to reports, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex plan to settle in the Cotswolds, an affluent countryside region in south-central England, located about two hours outside London. Archie and Lilibet are reportedly set to begin classes at a private school in the U.K., though the school has not been publicly named. PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE ARRIVE IN UK WITH KIDS, MARKING DRAMATIC RETURN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT In a report published Monday, royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Page Six that parents in the Cotswolds area received warning letters from school officials after Harry and Markle "approached multiple schools" for Archie and Lilibet ahead of their move. The letters reportedly reminded families of privacy rules surrounding students and high-profile families. PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE WON’T ‘HIJACK’ PRINCE GEORGE’S HISTORIC ETON DEBUT, ROYAL EXPERT SAYS "The message sent to families essentially said that, from time to time, some families joining the school may attract a greater level of public or media interest," Schofield told the outlet. The message also reportedly noted that the school wanted to preserve a "safe, happy, and private environment" for all students. MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK RETURN POSES PALACE CONTROL ‘NIGHTMARE,’ EXPERT WARNS "It then reminded parents and carers not to photograph or film other children without permission, or share photographs, information or details about pupils or their families on social media," Schofield said. Page Six did not identify the school that sent the letters, citing privacy concerns, but reported that it is not the school Archie and Lilibet are attending. PRINCE WILLIAM 'NO LONGER RECOGNIZES' PRINCE HARRY AS SECURITY BATTLE LEAVES DUKE 'CLOSE TO TEARS': EXPERT Harry and Markle have long tried to shield their children from uncontrolled public exposure. The couple has previously skipped the traditional royal baby photo call, limited public images of their children and raised security concerns around U.K. visits. However, royal experts told Fox News Digital that school life presents a different challenge because it places Archie and Lilibet’s privacy partly in the hands of other parents, classmates and the broader community. PRINCE WILLIAM LIKELY 'LIVID' OVER MEGHAN MARKLE'S 'TASTELESS' PHOTOS AT PRINCESS DIANA'S HOME: EXPERT Schofield, who also spoke to Fox News Digital about the couple’s return to Britain, said the school warnings underscore how difficult it may be for Harry and Markle to manage their children’s privacy in everyday settings. "School introduces an enormous number of variables Harry and Meghan cannot control," the host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" said. "Other parents have phones. Children have friends. There are school events, sporting fixtures, birthday parties, drop-offs, and pick-ups," Schofield added. "You cannot manage a school community like a communications operation." Schofield noted that the letter she had seen was "deliberately vague" but explained that the reminders were likely not unusual on their own. However, she argued that the attention surrounding Harry and Markle will change the dynamic for other families. "None of those requests are unreasonable," Schofield continued. "Archie and Lili deserve exactly the same opportunity as every other child to go to school without feeling watched. But inevitably, when one family attracts this level of global attention, the entire school community becomes more conscious of what it photographs, posts, and discusses." "Other families are effectively being asked to adjust their behavior because Harry and Meghan have arrived," she added. PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FACE 'SUSSEX CIRCUS' AS PRINCE GEORGE PREPARES FOR ETON: EXPERT While speaking with Fox News Digital, royal expert Hilary Fordwich pointed out that Markle posted photos of Archie and Lilibet on her own social media, sharing her view that it was "beyond hypocritical to on the one hand want ‘privacy’ yet on the other hand, monetize their family." While Markle has shared photos of her children on Instagram, they are often pictured from behind, with their faces hidden or in carefully chosen images. The former "Suits" star’s representative previously defended Markle’s approach in a statement to Newsweek. "The Duchess has always been clear that there is a distinction between sharing moments from her life and exposing her children to public scrutiny," her spokesperson said in June. articles.title: Gasly loses Monaco podium after McLaren and Red Bull win appeals
articles.summary: McLaren and Red Bull win their appeals against the result of the Monaco Grand Prix after a controversy over multiple incorrect pit-lane speeding penalties.
articles.body:
McLaren and Red Bull have won their appeals against the result of the Monaco Grand Prix after a controversy over multiple incorrect pit-lane speeding penalties.

The victory means Alpine's Pierre Gasly loses the podium he was awarded after an appeal by the French team that overturned two five-second penalties.

That means Gasly, who finished third on the road, is dropped back to the seventh place he received in the official results.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar is returned to third place and McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth, with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad moving up to fifth and sixth.

However, the verdict does not fully address the multiple effects of a series of pit-lane speeding penalties.

These affected the results of many drivers in the race, including Mercedes' George Russell.

The Briton was dropped out of the points for a penalty he received for not correctly serving a pit-lane speeding penalty.

The court of appeal decision rests on its conclusion that the parameters for measuring a limit could not be changed in the midst of a grand prix weekend once competitors had been informed of them.

The discrepancy between the official F1 measurement and the possible shorter distance did not mean that the official measurement was incorrect, the court said.

The finding was that, while it was concluded after the race that a shorter line was possible, "what sporting fairness absolutely precludes is the retrospective replacement, after competitors have calibrated and competed against it, of the common event-wide calibration parameter itself by a different geometric or measurement approach for the purpose of re-adjudicating an individual competitor's result".

The controversy arose from the fact that there was a 77-centimetre discrepancy between the officially measured distance of the pit lane and the real shortest route a driver could legally take.

It was established at Alpine's appeal that Gasly had not exceeded the pit-lane speeding limit by this new measurement, which was why the penalty was overturned.

However, McLaren appealed on the grounds of sporting fairness and their own competitive interests, as Piastri had lost two points as a consequence of the situation.

The Australian was one of the drivers who did serve a five-second pit-lane speeding penalty.

Alpine said in a statement: "While we disagree with the decision, and still fully maintain that car 10 (Gasly) did not exceed the pit-lane speed limit at any point during the race, the team acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris.

"While the result is not what we had hoped for, as we feel that we have been unjustly punished, the team is firmly focused on continuing to improve its performance on track and remains in a close and very competitive championship fight."
authors: Andrew Benson - F1 Correspondent at Monza

articles.title: Tiffany Haddish once lived out of her car and survived on $500 a month; after a stranger told her to buy property with every movie paycheck, she now owns about 17
articles.summary: Comedian and actor Tiffany Haddish says an unexpected conversation with an accountant changed the way she thought about money and property. Today, she.
articles.body: Comedian and actor Tiffany Haddish says an unexpected conversation with an accountant changed the way she thought about money and property. Today, she owns about 17 properties, but her approach to real estate began after years of financial uncertainty.Haddish recently spoke about her property investments during a live recording of the podcast 'Family Trips With the Meyers Brothers', Realtor reported. Seth Meyers and his brother, Josh Meyers, asked her about the kind of holidays she enjoys. Haddish said she likes travelling in groups and still uses Groupon to find discounted trips.One such trip took her to China and Japan. It was during that group holiday that she met an accountant who gave her advice that stayed with her. The accountant suggested she read “The Weekend Millionaire’s Secrets to Investing in Real Estate: How to Become Wealthy in Your Spare Time”, by Mike Summey and Roger Dawson.The accountant told her “If you’re doing movies and you think you’re going to make it, when you start making money, buy a piece of property every year for 15 years. No matter what happens with your career, you’ll be successful. They can never cancel you or stop you,” Haddish recalled.Haddish’s Real Estate JourneyHaddish said she followed that advice by buying property when she earned money from her acting career. She now has “like 17” properties in her portfolio and said she buys one whenever she stars in a movie.She also explained why she believes owning land can provide financial security. “If you have land, you’ll be a multimillionaire, even with 10 properties,” she said.Her current property holdings are a major change from the period when she struggled to find stable housing. Haddish has previously spoken about experiencing homelessness during the early part of her comedy career. She has also discussed spending time in foster care as a child.One of the people who helped her during that difficult period was fellow comedian Kevin Hart. Haddish spoke about this in a 2024 appearance on “This Life of Mine With James Cordon”.Kevin Hart Helped Her Find HomeAt the time, Haddish was performing sketch comedy shows with Hart at the Laugh Factory in Los Angeles. Hart noticed that her car was filled with her belongings and began to suspect that she was experiencing homelessness.Haddish said she tried to avoid discussing her situation with him. She would arrive late because she did not want other people to see her car and realise that she was living in it.“I would show up late. I didn’t want nobody to see my car. I would park a little farther away, or I would pull up and let the valet take the car, but I would pull up late so nobody would see,” she said.Hart eventually confronted the situation. He gave Haddish $300 that night, which she used to pay for a hotel room. He then connected her with a real estate agent who could help her find a place to live.The apartment she eventually found was far from ideal. Haddish said it needed extensive work and described its condition as poor.“It needed so much work,” she said. “It was disgusting, and I looked around and I was like, ‘Wow.’ I saw roaches. It was bad.” Despite its condition, the apartment gave her an affordable place to stay. The rent was $500 a month, so Haddish decided to take it.“I still have that place,” she confirmed in 2024. “I still have it. I had to fix it up myself and I still got it.”Paying Off Her First HouseHaddish later used a similar focus on property when she started earning more from acting. In a 2022 interview with Cosmopolitan, she described how she bought her first house after appearing on “The Carmichael Show” in 2015.She said people around her advised her to wait before buying a house. Haddish chose to move ahead because she wanted to make sure she could support herself and maintain the property.“Before we even got into Season 2 of ‘The Carmichael Show,’ I bought a house,” she said. “Everybody told me I should wait, but I didn’t care. I just knew I was going to have to always make enough money to take care of me and the house, and that’s what I did.”Her next acting projects helped her pay down the cost of the property. Haddish said she kept her personal spending low and was able to live comfortably on $500 a month during that period.“Between that show’s next season, the ‘Keanu’ movie, and making sure I can live comfortably off of $500 a month, I was able to pay off half the house,” she said.The money she earned from “Girls Trip” then helped her finish paying off the house. Haddish said she had been advised to use the money in other ways, but she chose to put it towards the property.“The ‘Girls Trip’ check was the final check. People told me to spend it other ways, but I used it to pay off the house because I was always afraid of being homeless again,” she saidAlthough Haddish now has a surplus of money because of her success, she has said she remains conscious of her finances. She also told Cosmopolitan that she would eventually like to retire and buy a ranch in Wyoming.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: Richard O'Sullivan, ‘Man About The House’ actor passes away at the age of 82
articles.summary: Richard O'Sullivan, best known for playing Robin Tripp in the 1970s sitcoms ‘Man About the House’ and Robin's Nest’, has passed away at the age of 82..
articles.body: Richard O'Sullivan, best known for playing Robin Tripp in the 1970s sitcoms ‘Man About the House’ and Robin's Nest’, has passed away at the age of 82. Over his career, he also took on notable roles in ‘Doctor at Large’, ‘Dick Turpin’, and the 1980s sitcom ‘Me and My Girl’, sharing the screen with Tim Brooke-Taylor, Joanne Ridley, and Joan Sanderson.Richard O'Sullivan passes away at Brinsworth HouseAccording to BBC, O'Sullivan passed away with close family by his side at Brinsworth House, the Royal Variety Charity's care home in west London, where he had made his home for the past 23 years.Royal Variety Charity pays tribute to Richard O'SullivanGiles Cooper of the Royal Variety Charity paid tribute in a statement, saying: "Richard O'Sullivan was a master of effortless charm and impeccable comic timing, bringing pure warmth, wit, and unforgettable joy to millions of living rooms as a true giant of British television." Cooper further noted that O'Sullivan would be "sorely missed by us all at the Royal Variety Charity".Richard O'Sullivan's son remembers him fondlyThe actor's son, James O'Sullivan, shared his own tribute, saying: "My dad was as funny and charming in real life as he appeared on our TV screens over the years. Although much of his career happened before I was born, I was fortunate enough to be able to enjoy and witness his incredible talents on the countless re-runs of his shows that made him the respected and loved actor that he was." He also expressed gratitude to the staff at Brinsworth House for their "love, kindness and care".Richard O'Sullivan's most memorable TV rolesSet around a man cohabiting with two single women in a London flat, a fairly daring concept for its time, ‘Man About the House’ ran for six series on ITV, with O'Sullivan starring alongside Paula Wilcox, Sally Thomsett, Yootha Joyce, and Brian Murphy. In ‘Me and My Girl’, he played a different role altogether, that of a widower bringing up his teenage daughter.Richard O'Sullivan's early life and career beginningsO'Sullivan, born in London in 1944, began acting as a child in the 1950s and 60s, taking on uncredited parts in dramas as early as 1953. He later featured in ‘Raiders of the River’, the Children's Film Foundation's debut serial, and in 1956 appeared in Sir Peter Hall's staging of ‘Love's Labour's Lost’ at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford. His credits also include the 1961 drama Spare the Rod, a social commentary starring Max Bygraves and Donald Pleasance about a teacher working in a deprived, challenging area, in which O'Sullivan portrayed a rebellious, difficult student in his final year. After building steady momentum with dramatic parts, including playing Pharaoh Ptolemy XIII in 1963's ‘Cleopatra’ alongside Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, he shifted towards comedy, appearing in shows like ‘The Ronnie Barker Playhouse’ in 1968 and ‘The Galton’ and ‘Simpson Comedy’ the year after.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Sydney Sweeney y Scooter Braun derrochan amor y complicidad en el Festival de Venecia
articles.standfirst: La actriz ha acudido como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty
articles.summary: La actriz ha acudido como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney es, sin duda, la actriz del momento. Sin embargo, esta vez no es tendencia por algún proyecto profesional, sino por su aparición pública con su novio, el empresario Scooter Braun. Ambos han acaparado todas las miradas en el Festival de Cine de Venecia 2026, donde han sido pillados compartiendo besos, miradas cómplices y un romántico paseo en góndola por los icónicos canales venecianos. La protagonista de ‘Euphoria’, que asiste al certamen cinematográfico como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty, aprovechó el viaje para celebrar su primer año de relación con Braun. A ambos se les vio muy sonrientes y relajados en todo momento, ajenos por completo a las cámaras de los fotógrafos mientras recorrían la ciudad tanto en transporte acuático como a pie. La historia de amor entre Sydney Sweeney y Scooter Braun comenzó con un auténtico flechazo en Venecia en junio de 2025, la misma ciudad en la que hoy celebran su primer aniversario. Ambos coincidieron como invitados en la lujosa e íntima boda de Jeff Bezos y Lauren Sánchez. La química entre la intérprete estadounidense y el mánager musical fue inmediata; de hecho, fuentes cercanas revelaron a portales como Page Six que Braun quedó fascinado tras conocerla. Después de ese fin de semana, comenzaron a verse con mayor frecuencia en Estados Unidos. Fue el medio Star quien destapó las primeras alarmas en septiembre de 2025 al reportar citas discretas en Nueva York y Los Ángeles. Durante esos meses, el entorno de la actriz aseguraba que preferían tomarse las cosas con calma y mantener un perfil bajo, especialmente por el revuelo mediático debido a la diferencia de edad y la fama de Braun. Finalmente, la pareja decidió dejar de esconderse e hizo pública su relación asistiendo juntos a la premiere de la nueva temporada de ‘Euphoria’. Poco después, oficializaron su amor en redes sociales.

articles.title: Harano Sur: Uttam Kumar at 100
articles.summary: At a hundred, Uttam Kumar, the Mahanayak or great hero of Bengali cinema, is the most agreed-upon man in Bengal. The agreement conceals a long negotia.
articles.body: At a hundred, Uttam Kumar, the Mahanayak or great hero of Bengali cinema, is the most agreed-upon man in Bengal. The agreement conceals a long negotiation, in which Bengal accepted certain things about him, refused others outright, and has still not accepted the one obligation that matters.The centenary arrived on schedule on September 3 and with better than usual paraphernalia: statues garlanded at Tollygunge, the home of the Bengali film industry, and at Ahiritola, the north Kolkata street where he was born; a twenty-foot cutout outside the iconic single-screen Bijoli cinema; a padayatra with artistes; LED vans doing the rounds; an exhibition of booklets and behind-the-scenes stills at Nandan, the state-run film centre; and a commemorative stamp and cover from the Department of Posts.And, beyond the day itself, the apparatus of a year: a foundation stone in New Town for a film centre on three acres; a twenty-member advisory board with the Chief Minister as chief patron; a year-long calendar; and a festival opening, inevitably, with Nayak, Satyajit Ray's study of a matinee idol, written for him.The Prime Minister posted a tribute in the morning and directed everyone to what he had said about the actor on Mann Ki Baat, his monthly radio address, the previous Sunday: that he had kept working through early failure, and should be admired for it. All of this is true, and almost none of it is interesting, because perseverance is the one quality you can commemorate without showing anybody a film.The more useful question on a hundredth birth anniversary is not what Bengal loved about Uttam Kumar. Bengal has been answering that compulsively since July 1980, when he died. The more interesting question is what Bengal was prepared to accept from him, and what it was not.From Flop Master General to MahanayakBegin with the acceptance, because it was neither instant nor free.Arun Kumar Chattopadhyay was born on 3 September 1926 at his maternal home on Ahiritola Street, in north Kolkata, the son of a man who ran the projector at the Metro cinema, which is to say that he came to the cinema through the back of the hall.He matriculated in the second division, took a clerk's job at the Port Commissioners on two hundred and seventy-five rupees a month, changed his screen name three times before one finally stuck, and by twenty-six had accumulated enough failure for the trade to nickname him the Flop Master General, a joke reportedly performed to his face on studio floors. Then came Nirmal Dey's Basu Paribar in 1952 and Sharey Chuattor in 1953, then Agni Pariksha in 1954, and a Bengal that had laughed at him for four years decided, within two, that he was the only face it wanted to look at.What it had decided to look at was itself, improved.The Bengali Uttam Kumar played was urban, salaried, educated, courteous and emotionally contained, a man who could be poor without being coarse and prosperous without becoming a boor, and he arrived exactly when a post-Partition middle class, remade by the 1947 division of Bengal and the refugees it drove west, needed evidence that such a man could still exist in Calcutta.The Encyclopaedia of Indian Cinema puts it more precisely than most tributes will this week, noting that his early romances revived the humanist tradition of the bhadralok, Bengal's respectable, educated middle class, while quietly discarding some of its more conservative furniture. He was a lover who did not chase; he waited, in Saptapadi, and returned much later to the wreckage, in Jatugriha. He made room for his heroines instead of rescuing them. Bengal accepted him because he flattered it in a register it recognised as good taste, which is the only kind of flattery the bhadralok has ever accepted.Three things Bengal withheldHaving granted him that, it began withholding other things.First, the ordinary latitude it might have extended to a private citizen. In 1963 he left the house he shared with Gauri Devi, whom he had married in 1948 and never divorced, and lived for the next seventeen years with the actress Supriya Devi. The audience that had built a cult around his on-screen restraint then conducted a running commentary on the arrangement for the rest of his life and a good while after it. Bengal was happy to watch him play a murderer in Kuhak, a rotting landlord in Stree, a bought politician in Bagh Bondi Khela. What it would not do was allow the man anything the character might have got away with.Second, it withheld the national career.He turned down Bees Saal Baad, turned down the second lead in Sangam, and then, in 1967, produced his own Hindi debut, Chhoti Si Mulaqat, a remake of Agni Pariksha with Vyjayanthimala in place of Suchitra Sen, his partner in the original and the other half of Bengali cinema's definitive screen couple. It failed so spectacularly that it left him close to bankruptcy. Bombay took him properly only once, with Shakti Samanta's Amanush in 1975, shot in Bengali and Hindi at the same time, which ran for the better part of two years and became the biggest hit of his career; when the same team tried again with Ananda Ashram, the Bengali version ran for months and the Hindi one died.There is no evidence that Bengal mourned any of this. A Mahanayak who belonged equally to Bombay would have stopped being quite so completely Bengal's property, and one of the uses of Uttam Kumar was precisely that he proved Bengal did not need Bombay's permission to produce a star.Third, and most instructively, Bengal withheld the right to be anybody else.On 23 September 1976, All India Radio dropped Birendra Krishna Bhadra's Mahishasuramardini, the recital that had woken Bengal before dawn every Mahalaya since the 1930s, on the day that opens the Durga Puja season. In its place came a new programme narrated by Uttam Kumar and scored by Hemanta Mukherjee, known outside Bengal as Hemant Kumar, which is to say by the two most beloved voices in the province. Listeners stoned Akashvani Bhavan, All India Radio's Kolkata headquarters. The switchboard was overwhelmed, demonstrations were held in Calcutta and elsewhere, the ministry was forced to climb down, Bhadra was restored, and the new version was exiled to Sashthi, the sixth day of the Puja, where it has survived ever since as a curiosity. It took Bengal roughly a fortnight to reject the most popular man it had ever produced, on the one occasion he stepped outside the frame it had built for him. He apologised. He did not try again.Worshipped, but not readThe most consequential withholding, however, came from his own constituency's clerisy.Bengal in his lifetime had a critical establishment that treated popular cinema as an embarrassment to be tolerated in the interests of the box office. The result was that the first actor in India to win the National Award for Best Actor, given to him in 1968, the first year of the category, for Antony Firingee and Ray's Chiriyakhana, generated a myth and remarkably little scholarship. Sayandeb Chowdhury, whose 2021 book remains the only serious critical biography, describes a star kept in a kind of solitary confinement by his own fame, and notes how little Bengal's learned circles bothered to understand his range, his production work or his stewardship of an entire industry.Ray, who wrote Nayak for him and about him, had no such difficulty and said plainly that there would not be another like him. It is a peculiar arrangement in which the director is canonised, the star is worshipped, and only one of them gets read.The industry's balance sheetThat stewardship is the part of the legend the garlands rarely reach.Uttam Kumar produced films from 1957, directed from 1966, composed music for Kal Tumi Aleya, and in 1968 left the existing actors' body to set up Shilpi Sangshad, a welfare organisation for technicians and small artistes, running it until his death. When the fund ran dry, he made a film to replenish it: Bon Palashir Padabali in 1973, which he directed himself while persuading some of the industry's biggest names to work for nothing. It went on to become the year's highest earner.He was not merely the ornament of Bengali cinema. For thirty years he was, to an extraordinary extent, its balance sheet, which is why the industry did not simply mourn him in 1980 but visibly began to falter without him, and why Anandabazar Patrika, Bengal's largest Bengali daily, could compress the event into two words: Cholochitre Indrapatan, the fall of Indra in the cinema, which is Bengali for the toppling of a colossus.Why governments prefer birthdaysWhich brings us to the present negotiation, and to what is being accepted this week.For four decades, remembering Uttam Kumar was centred on 24 July, the anniversary of his death, and took place largely in a folk register: Shilpi Sangshad's own festival at Nandan, the retrospectives, the television reruns, the Mahanayak Samman that the previous government instituted in 2012 and handed out every July at Uttam Mancha, the south Kolkata auditorium named after him. The centenary completes a migration that has been under way for some years, from the day he died to the day he was born, which is to say from a mourning that belonged to the audience to an anniversary that can belong to the state.Governments prefer birthdays. Birthdays are about arrival.Every government has taken its turn. The Left Front, then in power in West Bengal, put up the Tollygunge statue in 1993. The metro station was renamed and the first stamp issued in 2009. The Trinamool Congress government created the award in 2012. A BJP government four months old in Bengal, looking for a Bengali inheritance nobody can reasonably contest, has now given him a year, a board, a stamp, three acres and a padayatra, with the Prime Minister supplying the moral.Nobody in this sequence needs to be insincere, which is precisely the difficulty. Uttam Kumar is loved almost without exception, and a figure loved without exception is available to everybody. Standing next to that smile has never cost a politician a single vote.The vaults nobody has openedWhat none of them has accepted is custody.In 2018, when the Film Heritage Foundation brought its restoration workshop to the Kolkata International Film Festival, its founder, the archivist and filmmaker Shivendra Singh Dungarpur, pointed out that Bengal had lost every silent film it made between 1918 and the early thirties and that his foundation had identified more than a hundred Bengali titles in need of urgent rescue. On that list sits Harano Sur, the 1957 film Uttam Kumar produced himself, the year's biggest earner, whose title translates as the lost tune.Soumitra Chatterjee, Ray's other great leading man and the only serious rival Uttam Kumar had for the Bengali audience, was asked about the same crisis and said he doubted whether the classics of Barua, the Devdas director P.C. Barua, or Uttam Kumar, or even his own early work, could still be saved. Eight years later, the state's own information secretary describes Uttam Mancha as dilapidated, the film directorate's brief already includes restoration of the holdings in government vaults, and yet the most basic public question remains unanswered: which of Uttam Kumar's two hundred and eleven films survive as negatives, which survive as scratched prints, which exist only in some distributor's family cupboard, and which are simply gone?Meanwhile, the state says the purpose of all this is to introduce him to a generation that missed him.That generation's actual access too often consists of YouTube uploads mastered from video cassettes, and Oti Uttam, the Bengali director Srijit Mukherji's 2024 film in which the Mahanayak appears as a ghost assembled from footage drawn from fifty-four of his own films, with his voice cloned by an American AI company because there was no other way left to make him speak a new line. The exercise cost about a crore and a half.Sit with that for a moment: a generation that has rarely had the chance to see a clean print of Chowringhee has already paid to watch a synthetic reconstruction of the man who was in it.The appetite is proven. The supply is a policy failure.The test is 2036So let the padayatra proceed, and let the foundation stone be laid. The test of this centenary will not be what gets unveiled between now and next September, but whether, in 2036, a nineteen-year-old in Barrackpore can watch a properly restored Jatugriha on a legal platform, in a decent transfer, subtitled by somebody who knows Bengali.Publish the vault inventory. Fund restoration before construction. Clear the rights, which are scattered across heirs and defunct distributors and grow harder to trace every year.Bengal has spent a century deciding what it would and would not accept from Uttam Kumar. The one thing he actually needs from us now is the one obligation we have still not accepted.The lost tune (harano sur) stays lost, cutout notwithstanding.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: El llamativo momento entre Máximo Huerta, Iván Redondo y Cristina Pardo en ‘La Mesa’: “Mal rollo”
articles.standfirst: Antena 3 estrenó este nuevo programa con la expresentadora de ‘Más Vale Tarde’ al frente
articles.summary: Antena 3 estrenó este nuevo programa con la expresentadora de ‘Más Vale Tarde’ al frente
articles.body: Antena 3 estrenó este miércoles, 2 de septiembre, ‘La Mesa’, un nuevo programa para esta temporada de la mano de Cristina Pardo y lo hizo con colaboradores de alto calado como Iván Redondo y Máximo Huerta. Pues bien, entre ellos tres se vivió un momento curioso, ya que Huerta le pidió a la presentadora cambiarse de silla tras haber sido usada por Iván Redondo. En primera instancia, apareció Redondo, quien se pronunció acerca de la gestión que está haciendo el Gobierno y su equipo con lo que pasa en Ceuta, algo en lo que Huerta también opinó en la misma dirección. No obstante, el escritor, una vez sentado en la otra silla del plató, dijo lo siguiente a Cristina Pardo, instándole a cambiar el mueble: “Me quiero cambiar de silla. En la silla de Iván Redondo, no. La de Iván Redondo, no. Me lo vas a permitir. Esto me va a dar mala suerte". Cabe recordar que Huerta coincidió con Redondo en el Gobierno cuando fue nombrado ministro de Cultura y Deporte, algo en lo que tan solo estuvo siete días, ya que se dio a conocer que esquivó un pago de más de 200.00 euros a Hacienda. Esto causó la respuesta de la presentadora del nuevo programa de Antena 3: “Tú coincidiste con Iván Redondo en el Gobierno cuando él era jefe de gabinete, ¿no?". A ello respondió Máximo Huerta de manera afirmativa: "En uno de los momentos más fuertes de mi vida y al sentarme me ha dado un mal rollo... y por eso te lo he pedido así, que como no hay falso directo ni nada". “Pero, ¿qué pasa? ¿Él participó en tu salida del Gobierno?", apostilló la televisiva, a lo que el de Utiel respondió: "Uno de los peores días de mi vida es Iván Redondo y yo conectando con Alsina. Con lo cual digo 'joder, qué noche, querida”. "Entonces es como tener un déjà vu horroroso", sentenció Cristina Pardo al respecto, antes de presentar a la siguiente colaboradora, que será Ivana Rodríguez, la hermana de Georgina Rodriguez

articles.title: Taylor Frankie Paul says she got engaged on ‘Bachelorette’ season that never aired
articles.summary: Taylor Frankie Paul revealed that she got engaged while filming her season of “The Bachelorette,” which was pulled from the air just days before premiere.
articles.body: Taylor Frankie Paul revealed that she got engaged while filming her season of “The Bachelorette,” which was pulled from the air just days before premiere. Paul discussed the drama surrounding her shelved “Bachelorette” season in the upcoming Season 5 of “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” as seen in a clip from the show shared by the Hulu podcast “Get Real” on Sept. 3. The clip began with Paul appearing to deny to castmates Jessi Draper, Mayci Neeley and Mikayla Matthews that she was intimate with anyone in one of the fantasy suites on “The Bachelorette.” Draper mentioned “The Bachelorette” suitor whom Paul reportedly chose, Doug Mason, without saying his name. She asked Paul if she ever thought Mason “looks like Dakota,” in reference to Paul’s ex-boyfriend, Dakota Mortensen, with whom Paul shares a son. “I didn’t start thinking that until people said it around me,” Paul said. “They have the same initials,” Draper responded. “They’re both from Idaho. It’s so weird.” Paul then left her “Mormon Wives” castmates stunned when she revealed how her experience filming “The Bachelorette” ended. “And yes, he did get down on one knee and proposed, which I was shocked,” she said. Paul said she accepted the proposal. “And then I come home,” she said. She said she returned to Utah and began texting Mortensen. “I don’t know how it led to it, but he came over,” Paul said. Paul’s season of “The Bachelorette” was canceled in March after TMZ published a video reportedly from an altercation between Paul and Mortensen in 2023 that led to her arrest. Paul later pled guilty in abeyance to aggravated assault, court records obtained by NBC News show. The former couple was also involved in a domestic violence investigation earlier this year stemming from several alleged incidents from 2024 to 2026, police confirmed to NBC News. Reps for Mortensen and Paul declined to comment at the time. In April, the Salt Lake County District Attorney’s Office said neither Paul nor Mortensen would face new charges. Filming for Season 5 of “Mormon Wives” was paused amid the investigation but picked back up around late April. “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” will return for Season 5 on Sept. 10.

articles.title: Steve Irwin’s Cameraman Details His Final Moments With Stingray Amid 20th Anniversary of His Death
articles.summary: Steve Irwin‘s cameraman, Justin Lyons, recently recalled the tragic moment a stingray fatally pierced the chest of the late conservationist while they were f...
articles.body:
Steve Irwin's cameraman, Justin Lyons, recounted the tragic moment when a stingray fatally pierced the late conservationist's chest while filming a documentary at the Great Barrier Reef.

Lyons shared that they had filmed with stingrays many times before, but the final shot went awry when the stingray mistook Irwin for a tiger shark and started stabbing towards him with its tail.

Despite efforts to save him, Steve Irwin fell unconscious and passed away at age 44 after being pierced in the chest by the stingray, leaving his family and crew devastated.

Steve Irwin 's cameraman, Justin Lyons , recently recalled the tragic moment a stingray fatally pierced the chest of the late conservationist while they were filming a documentary at the Great Barrier Reef.

Lyons participated in a 60 Minutes Australia documentary titled Steve Irwin: A Wild Life , which aired on Wednesday, September 2, to mark 20 years since the man dubbed "The Crocodile Hunter" died.

In the documentary, Lyons shared that filming with stingrays was nothing new for the two men, as they'd done it "a hundred times before."

Before things took a turn for the worse on September 4, 2006, Lyons said he got multiple shots of the TV personality with a "massive" bull ray stingray. They then wanted to get the "final shot, which would be the opening shot, because "by now the stingray was calm," he said. However, it did not go as planned.

"The stingray is in front of me, buried in the sand. He swims up, swims over the top of it. It doesn't move. But as he's directly over the top of it, of course, it thought he was a tiger shark and started stabbing madly towards him with its tail," Lyons recounted. "The water just boiled. I couldn't see anything that was going on. Bubbles and thrashing and then all of a sudden it stopped, and the stingray swam away. The water calmed. So I just panned with the stingray … I let it go out of shot as I panned back to Steve. He came jumping up out of the water, screaming, and the water around him was now full of blood."

"He screamed out, 'It's punctured me lung.' I threw the camera into one of the rubber duckies, drag Steve into the boat," Lyons remembered. "His khaki shirt is open, and he's just got blood pouring out of a gash like that in his chest right over his heart. But he's conscious, and he says to me, looks me right in the eye, and he says, 'I'm dying.'"

The father of two — who shares Bindi , 28, and Robert , 22, with wife Terri — then fell unconscious as they went back to his boat, Croc One, where the crew attempted CPR on him for 45 minutes while they raced to Low Island.

"I just remember us putting in a massive effort to get him up the beach, put him in a little hut, and then I heard a chopper landing, and that was paramedics arriving, and I had this absolute sense of relief. I was like, 'Oh my god, they'll be able to bring him back to life. They will save him,'" Lyons said. "But within about 10 seconds of them being there, they just said, 'No, he's gone.' And then it really hit me. It was like absolute despair."

Over the years since his death at age 44, Terri, 62, Bindi, and Robert have honored Steve through their work at Australia Zoo.
